## Data

```{r}
zooplankton_data <- read.csv(here("Data/Temp/zoo_grouped.csv"))
phytoplankton_data <- read.csv(here("Data/Temp/phyto_grouped.csv"))
```

# Filter out samples (dates) with more than a certain amount of bad quality flags (S flags)

S flags indicate that the recorded abundance of an organism (here, our superior groups) in a sample may be inaccurate.

```{r}
head(zooplankton_data)
```

The more S quality flags there are in a sample, the more we can question the quality of the sample as a whole.

The following function discards samples where the percentage of S flags exceeds a certain threshold.

N.B. sometimes there are both good and bad quality flags for the same group in the same sample (because of the taxonomic grouping), so we simplify by computing the total (sum) abundance of the group in that case (if we keep the sample).

```{r}
filter_bad_quality <- function(plankton_data, quality_threshold) {
  plankton_data |>
    group_by(date) |>
    filter((sum(quality_flag == "S") / n()) <= quality_threshold) |>
    select(-quality_flag) |>
    group_by(date, superior_group) |>
    summarize(across(abundance, sum)) |>
    ungroup()
}
```

Here we use a threshold of zero to remove all samples where there is at least one bad quality flag (but it would also be possible to use a less strict threshold such as 0.1 or 0.5 for instance).

```{r}
zooplankton_data <- filter_bad_quality(zooplankton_data, 0)
phytoplankton_data <- filter_bad_quality(phytoplankton_data, 0)
```

# Filter out samples (dates) that contain only fish and decapod larvae

```{r}
zooplankton_data |>
  filter(date == as.Date("2024-04-08"))
```

Some zooplankton samples such as this one only contain fish larvae and decapod larvae, so we can confidently remove them (they were likely not supposed to be a part of this dataset).

```{r}
filter_fish_samples <- function(plankton_data) {
  plankton_data |>
    group_by(date) |>
    filter(!(all(superior_group %in% c("Fish_larva", "Decapod_larva")))) |>
    ungroup()
}
```

```{r}
zooplankton_data <- filter_fish_samples(zooplankton_data)
```

# Filter out superior groups that should be removed

For instance, benthic taxa. These have already been identified and grouped into the "REMOVE" superior group.

```{r}
zooplankton_data <- zooplankton_data |>
  filter(superior_group != "REMOVE")

phytoplankton_data <- phytoplankton_data |>
  filter(superior_group != "REMOVE")
```

# Export data

```{r}
write.csv(zooplankton_data, here("Data/Temp/zoo_filtered.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(phytoplankton_data, here("Data/Temp/phyto_filtered.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```
